conflicts_resolved.between: Execution (attempt folder + COMMIT file + MANIFEST), Storage (staging + objects + journal line as completion record), Integrity (merge.mjs into the shared tree)
conflicts_resolved.resolution: One commit record: a ledger line {task, epoch, step key, output hashes} written by commit.mjs, first wins, identical repeat is a no-op. No COMMIT file, no per-field journal, no merge.mjs: commit.mjs reads the current-epoch attempt folder's staging/ directly and writes the content-addressed store; git only records history with the ledger head.

conflicts_resolved.between: Execution (put.mjs as the child's write path, needing one shell permission) and Integrity/Storage (child has no Bash)
conflicts_resolved.resolution: Child has no shell. It writes drafts to staging/ with Write; commit.mjs validates, rejects torn or invalid files with a reason code, and harvest.mjs takes reader results from transcripts. put.mjs dropped.

conflicts_resolved.between: Execution events.jsonl, Integrity ledger.jsonl, Storage journal.jsonl, Shape group-start ledger lines, Completeness incidents/<writer>.jsonl
conflicts_resolved.resolution: One hash-chained ledger run/ledger.jsonl, appended only through lib.mjs under a lock; events, commit records, incidents, meter readings and refusals are typed lines in it.

conflicts_resolved.between: Storage control/epoch and Execution run/coord.json plus per-task epochs
conflicts_resolved.resolution: Kept run/coord.json (ce) and the task table's epoch; control/epoch dropped.

conflicts_resolved.between: Storage status.mjs and Execution status.mjs; Execution endturn.mjs, meter.mjs, intent.mjs
conflicts_resolved.resolution: One status.mjs with --reconcile and --endturn; meter recording folded into spend.mjs; intents into lib.mjs.

conflicts_resolved.between: Integrity perm-audit.mjs and Storage audit.mjs; Evidence search-log.js
conflicts_resolved.resolution: One audit.mjs after every turn: read audit/taint, privilege and URL audit, TURN-END note check, and the search log.

conflicts_resolved.between: Storage tms.mjs labels and Integrity certify/low-water labels and their status lattices
conflicts_resolved.resolution: One label script tms.mjs over one graph: card statuses pending, witnessed, confirmed, unverifiable, rejected, superseded; node labels STALE > PENDING > JUDGMENT > IN; promote.mjs is the only status writer.

conflicts_resolved.between: Storage snap.mjs and Integrity snapshot.mjs; snapshots in the field folder (D1-05, D8-02) vs outside git (D2-09)
conflicts_resolved.resolution: One snap.mjs; snapshots in .snapshots/ outside git and outside every attempt folder.

conflicts_resolved.between: Shape capacity-check.js run by the child (who has no shell) and the watcher
conflicts_resolved.resolution: The capacity check runs in guard-hook.mjs before each reader start (true check-before-insert by the harness) and is repeated by the watcher each tick; no separate script.

conflicts_resolved.between: Evidence coverage.js and Completeness estimate.js
conflicts_resolved.resolution: One recapture.mjs with a source mode and a hazard mode.

conflicts_resolved.between: Completeness canary-check.js and Integrity selftest hook test
conflicts_resolved.resolution: The hook canary is part of selftest.mjs.

conflicts_resolved.between: Mappings on restart limit (D3-08: two; D1-09, D4-07: one)
conflicts_resolved.resolution: R = 1, then the owner chooses a changed input.

conflicts_resolved.between: Mappings on sleep (D4-06 exits; D1-02, D3-06 shift deadlines)
conflicts_resolved.resolution: Shift deadlines and log the pause; every process resumes on wake.

conflicts_resolved.between: Frame's waves and per-task admission (D1-08)
conflicts_resolved.resolution: Per-task admission when a slot frees; a wave survives only as the owner's checkpoint.

conflicts_resolved.between: Frame layer 3 (one trusted class, consumers read only trusted) and the mappings
conflicts_resolved.resolution: Two grades (witnessed by script, confirmed = measured judgment), unverifiable never passes; sessions labelled by what they read; trusted-only readers are pack freeze, fresh reviewer, synthesis, coordinator.

conflicts_resolved.between: Frame layer 6 (node capacity is the window budget; fan-out computed) and the B+/square-root mappings
conflicts_resolved.resolution: Two capacities (pack C_node, spend A_leaf); B+ governs only what must share a window; windows follow the square-root law; leaves stay expertise lanes and the computed bound is a check.

conflicts_resolved.between: Frame layer 2 (synthesis is a derived view) and D7-11/D6-08
conflicts_resolved.resolution: The synthesis table is a view; a cross-field adjudication is a model-written object under the citation constraints.

conflicts_resolved.between: Storage (dismissal out-list matching later) and Evidence (dismissals.js pilot)
conflicts_resolved.resolution: dismissals.mjs is pilot, as P15 is the programme's founding mistake; matching runs over whatever cards exist.

conflicts_resolved.between: Integrity (separation of duty: coordinator starts checkers) and Execution (coordinator turns)
conflicts_resolved.resolution: The coordinator starts checker helpers; the watcher exits non-urgently on a ready batch and promote.mjs reads verdicts from the checker's transcript.

conflicts_resolved.between: Evidence pilot list (rescreen, second-opinion) and the small-pilot rule
conflicts_resolved.resolution: The exclusion re-screen and second-opinion.mjs moved to later; F2 is decided after the pilot's reviews.

conflicts_resolved.between: Script file extensions (.mjs in L1-L3, .js in L4-L6)
conflicts_resolved.resolution: All .mjs; the existing cost.js prototype is renamed cost.mjs.

left_out: Backup (speculative) tasks for stragglers: they double tokens
Consensus, two-phase commit and distributed locks: one coordinator plus epochs suffice; a blocking protocol stalls on a sleeping session
Voting or N-version redundancy across same-model instances: failures correlate
Per-sentence information-flow labels: a window is one flow; session-level low-water mark used
Injection detection or filter lists: filtering in band is the root of injection; authority is bounded instead
Meta-analysis, funnel plots and GRADE upgrade domains: no common effect scale; upgrades would be self-assigned
Delphi or debate between same-model experts: conformity
B+ height, B-link latches, underflow merges, a scalability-law fit: nothing to gain with one inner node and three sessions
Contract-net bidding: sessions cannot estimate their own cost
A database engine: plain files merge and can be read by eye
Deleting or garbage-collecting anything during the run
FMEA risk priority numbers and fault trees: false precision; trees once a top event recurs
A separate Windows account for sessions: held as the fallback if the hook test fails
Exiting on sleep: deadlines shift instead
Put.mjs and a shell permission for the child
Currency of any kind: tokens only

Deferred to after the pilot: Smith's order, escrow from unit costs, redistribution of cross-field keys, source index and coupling, saturation stop-check, exclusion re-screen, second-opinion measurement, correct-rates, challenge, cooke, salvage, migrate, fracas, PDF extraction
for_the_owner: The go: nothing starts without it
F1 where the review runs: both forms in the pilot; default for 'no difference shown' is fresh
F2 the second expert: none until the pilot's reviews, then a second reviewer of the same pack plus the contrary-evidence reader
F3 a second provider's model for checks, scoring and extra completeness lenses
F4 the cap, the pilot allowance in tokens and the admission margin: without them nothing is admitted
F5 the Node fetch script, keeping local page snapshots outside git, and whether a PDF text package may be installed: without F5 every card is unverifiable and no certificate passes
Restart limit R = 1 (D3-08 would allow two)
Starting the fresh coordinator yourself at a quiet point after each hand-over
Keeping the PC awake: accept that sleep costs only time, or allow a power request
Memory reserve and N_max (two children until peak memory is measured)

All thresholds before the pilot: d0 per fault class, p1 and beta, SPRT p0/p1/alpha/beta, plants t of 3, coverage floor, completeness residual threshold, smallest effect of interest per measure, an action line per measure
Approvals: question lists, approach ids, field protocols, the analysis plan, the protocol model's property list, plan-time splits and dropped ranges
If the hook test fails: detective layer only or a separate Windows account; where deny rules live
Whether the single-session control runs twice (S2)
Whether the hand-over line is set by token count or weighted token cost
doubts: Length: 612 lines in all, 72 of them table rows (540 other lines), against 'about 520'. The section-9 table alone has 58 rows, because every problem has to have its own row.

Merging the logs into one ledger and letting commit.mjs read attempt folders directly, with no git merge, are my own simplifications. No layer designer proposed exactly this. Lock contention on the single ledger, including refusal lines from the hook, is assumed to be harmless and has not been measured.
The capacity check runs inside guard-hook.mjs, which assumes that each reader brief names its question ids in a form the hook can parse, and that hooks fire for Agent calls. Neither is verified.
Pilot calibration of the checker (14 seeds per J class plus as many clean items, so 112 checker items at d0 = 0.8) is a real token cost inside the pilot. Its size depends on the owner's d0.
The pilot list still has about 34 scripts. Each one guards a problem I judged high, but no per-problem severity rating was given, so the high/low cut is my judgment.

Figures quoted from cost.mjs (2.4 to 4.4 times the tokens for the F1 price; the plain law handing over about twice too often) and the completeness estimates (roughly 40 to 80, about 7) are computed from mostly guessed or contaminated inputs. They are labelled that way, but they are still numbers in the document.

The count of source checks (about 226 entries, about 26 looked up by web search) comes from the lengths of the check arrays and the 'overall' texts, which differ slightly per field (for example, D4's text says 37 citations but its array has 32 entries).

I read amendment 3, the result.json index, a compact index of all 103 mappings, every field's missing-risk titles and every source check's 'overall' text. I did not read each mapping's full text. Specific mechanisms come from the six layer specs as given.
